summary: BianLian is a likely Russia-based ransomware developer/deployer and data-extortion group active against US and Australian critical infrastructure since June 2022. It enters with RDP credentials bought from IABs, phishing or ProxyShell, implants a per-victim Go backdoor, and relies on PowerShell/cmd one-liners for defense impairment, discovery and credential theft. Since January 2024 it has run exfiltration-only extortion (no encryption), exfiltrating via FTP, Rclone and Mega.
uniqueTraits: Custom Go backdoor compiled per victim; Ngrok and modified Rsocks SOCKS5 tunnels
Registry edits disabling Sophos tamper protection (SAVEnabled/SEDEnabled/SAVService) and DISM removal of Defender
TightVNC service copied into SafeBoot\Network so it survives Safe Mode
Scheduled task as SYSTEM running rundll32 c:\programdata\netsh.dll,Entry; binaries/tasks named after Windows or security services
Exfiltration-only extortion since 2024, Rclone staged in programdata\vmware and Music folders

sources.title: #StopRansomware: BianLian Data Extortion Group (AA23-136A, updated Nov. 20, 2024)

chain.procedure: Logs in over RDP with compromised credentials likely bought from initial access brokers; phishing also used.
chain.noAtomicReason: Local catalogue has no atomic that reproduces an external logon with stolen VPN/RDP credentials; validate with authentication-log analytics (impossible travel, no-MFA VPN logons).

chain.procedure: Targets public-facing Windows and ESXi infrastructure, possibly using the Exchange ProxyShell chain (CVE-2021-34473, CVE-2021-34523, CVE-2021-31207).
chain.noAtomicReason: Local catalogue has no Windows atomic for exploiting this public-facing product/CVE; validate via perimeter/WAF and product logs instead.

chain.procedure: Downloads a custom Go backdoor built for each victim plus scanners and RMM software onto the foothold.

atomics.note: PowerShell download of a tool; backdoor itself is not reproduced

chain.procedure: Uses Ngrok and/or a modified Rsocks to build SOCKS5 tunnels from victim networks and mask C2 destinations.
Copies the TightVNC tvnserver service key into HKLM\...\SafeBoot\Network so remote access survives Safe Mode with Networking.

atomics.testName: Windows Add Registry Value to Load Service in Safe Mode with Network
atomics.note: Registers a service to load in Safe Mode with Network

chain.procedure: Activates the local Administrator (net user <admin> /active:yes), resets its password, and creates multiple domain admin (and Azure AD) accounts for persistence and lateral movement.

atomics.testName: Create a new Windows domain admin user
atomics.note: Create a new domain admin user

chain.procedure: Exploits CVE-2022-37969 (Windows CLFS driver) and likely Zerologon (exp.exe) to escalate.
chain.noAtomicReason: Catalogue has no CLFS (CVE-2022-37969) or Zerologon exploitation atomic; the only T1068 tests are BYOVD driver loads, which do not represent this procedure.

chain.procedure: Disables AMSI (amsiInitFailed), removes Defender with dism /Disable-Feature /FeatureName:Windows-Defender, and sets Sophos TamperProtection SAVEnabled/SEDEnabled/SAVService to 0 so Sophos can be uninstalled.

atomics.testName: Tamper with Windows Defender Registry - Reg.exe
atomics.note: reg.exe tampering of AV registry configuration

chain.procedure: Renames binaries and scheduled tasks after legitimate Windows services/security products, e.g. a SYSTEM task running rundll32 c:\programdata\netsh.dll,Entry; UPX packing.

atomics.testName: Creating W32Time similar named service using schtasks
atomics.note: Scheduled task named like a Windows service

chain.procedure: Runs Advanced Port Scanner, SoftPerfect Network Scanner, SharpShares (s.exe /ldap:all) and PingCastle; ping.exe -4 -n 1 sweeps.

atomics.testName: Enumerate All Network Shares with SharpShares
atomics.note: SharpShares enumeration of all network shares

chain.procedure: One-liner combining quser, [adsisearcher] computer/user counts, net user /domain, net group "domain admins" /domain, nltest /dclist and /domain_trusts; PowerShell lists processes, software and drives.

atomics.testName: Enumerate Active Directory Users with ADSISearcher
Windows - Discover domain trusts with nltest

chain.procedure: Loops tasklist to find lsass.exe and runs rundll32 comsvcs.dll MiniDump to \Windows\Temp\<file>.csv.
Runs a PE build of Impacket secretsdump (dump.exe -no-pass -just-dc) against the domain controller and attempts NTDS.dit access.

atomics.testName: Dump Active Directory Database with NTDSUtil

chain.procedure: findstr /spin "password" *.* to a file in the Music folder; SessionGopher to extract saved remote-access session credentials.

Before RDP, adds accounts to Remote Desktop Users, adds 'allow RemoteDesktop' netsh rules / enables the Remote Desktop rule group, sets RDP-Tcp UserAuthentication=0 and fAllowToGetHelp=1; then RDP and PsExec with valid accounts, SMB type-3 logons.

atomics.testName: Disable NLA for RDP via Command Prompt
Allow SMB and RDP on Microsoft Defender Firewall

chain.procedure: PowerShell scripts search for sensitive files and compress/encrypt them before exfiltration.

atomics.testName: Zip a Folder with PowerShell for Staging in Temp
atomics.note: PowerShell zip of a folder for staging

chain.procedure: Exfiltrates over FTP and with Rclone (installed in programdata\vmware and Music folders) and to Mega.

Exfiltrate data with rclone to cloud Storage - Mega (Windows)

chain.procedure: Before January 2024, encryptor.exe appended .bianlian and dropped 'Look at this instruction.txt'; since then extortion is exfiltration-only with notes threatening leaks, printed notes and phone calls.
